label: Claude Fable 5.2
output:
To the residents of Aughrim Terrace,

I'm in number 14. If this isn't about you, sorry for the bit of paper through your door, and you can stop reading here. If it is about you, keep going.

Somebody on this road has been putting their rubbish in my grey bin. Not the odd bit either. Full black bags, every week, for about a month now. Last Tuesday I got home from work at 3am and the lid wouldn't even close. Three bags in it that weren't mine, one of them full of nappies.

In case you don't know how it works, my bin is with Greenmount and it's charged by weight, 41c a kilo. My bill is normally around €25 for two months. The last one was €63.20. So I've paid nearly forty quid to get rid of someone else's rubbish, on a bartender's wages, in a rented house. I'm fuming, and I think that's fair enough.

It's not a mistake either. The bin has 14 painted on the lid in big white numbers.

I know it's someone on the terrace because one of the bags had a gas bill envelope in it with an Aughrim Terrace address. The name was torn off, which tells me whoever it is knows well what they're doing. A car was also seen pulling up at the bin on Tuesday evening.

I'm not looking for a row. I have to live here same as you. But I work nights, I'm coming and going at all hours, and I'm not a pushover. So it stops now. Simple as.

If you're stuck for a bin, knock on my door and ask. I'll tell you who to ring and how to set it up. It's not hard, and it's not dear if it's only your own rubbish going in.

If it keeps happening, the bin gets a padlock, and I'll be keeping a much closer eye on it on Tuesday nights.

Thanks to everyone else for reading.

No. 14

I left out that it was the fella across the road who saw the car, so he doesn't get dragged into it. Say the word if you'd rather he was mentioned.
